title: run_tty_answer waits forever when the prompt is slower than its 30s timeout, so a loaded machine hangs the full suite silently
body:
## What happens

`run_tty_answer` (`tests/lib/test_helper.bash`) sets `timeout 30`, waits for `[y/N]`, and sends the answer. If the prompt has not appeared within 30s, the first `expect` takes its `timeout { }` branch and sends nothing. `catch {expect eof}` then waits another 30s and gives up. `catch wait result` has no timeout at all, and the child is still sitting at its prompt reading `/dev/tty`, so it blocks forever.

**So a prompt that is merely slow hangs the whole suite, and nothing reports it.** There is no failure, no skip and no message; the run never ends.

## Measured

- **2026-09-18, vc's full suite at 1df5104** (`bin/devbin test all`, backgrounded, own TMPDIR) stopped at test 482, `at a terminal, fullcycle without --force shows what goes, asks once, and a y runs the cycle (0089)`, at about 00:00Z. At 06:44Z it had still not moved, and it was killed; 481 ok, 0 not ok before it. The machine was loaded that night: 481 tests took about 72 minutes, where the next morning's run did 923 in about 30.
- **2026-09-19, the same arm at 30a137d**, with no change to fullcycle, clean, fullcycle.bats or the helper since 1df5104: it passed on its own (3s), in its file (58/58, 64s), in an emulated gate context (`DEVBIN_GATE_TTY=0`, stdin `/dev/null`, output piped), and as test 482 of a full suite.
- **Mechanism driven:** the same arm, with only `set timeout 30` changed to `set timeout 1` in a scratch worktree, ran until `gtimeout 90` killed it (rc 124), with only `1..1` printed.

## Why it matters

It is the 0086 class: a suite that can block rather than fail. It also breaks the tree-lock protocol. A full suite is announced as a lock, and a hung one holds that lock indefinitely while looking like a run in progress.

## Fix shape (not prescribed)

A timeout waiting for the prompt must end the run as a FAILURE that names the arm. It should close or kill the spawn and exit non-zero with a message, so the arm reports `no [y/N] within Ns` instead of waiting on `wait`. The final wait needs a bound too, eg `expect eof` with a timeout, then `close` and `wait`. Drive it red first with the 1s timeout above: the arm must go from hanging to `not ok` naming the missing prompt. The other expect-based helpers should be checked for the same unbounded wait.

---

_Generated by Intent v3.0.3 from the issue canon. Do not edit this file -- it is rendered from the model, and `intent doctor` reports any hand-edit as skew._

## Resolution

**Fixed by dc at `749c4c0`, with the one remaining unbounded wait declared at `758d96e`; reviewed by vc and closed by dc on 2026-09-19.** `run_tty_answer` bounds both of its waits. If no `[y/N]` arrives within `DEVBIN_TEST_TTY_PROMPT_WAIT` seconds (default 120), or the command has not finished `DEVBIN_TEST_TTY_FINISH_WAIT` seconds after the answer (default 300), it kills the command's process group, closes the spawn, reaps it, and exits 124 naming the wait that ran out. The defaults are wide because a loaded machine is the case that hung. Only one wait is still unbounded, and it is declared at the helper: the final `wait` after `eof`, which a command that closes the pty and keeps running would block.

The two red-first arms are in `clean.bats`, beside 0090's. Each gives the command 8s of silence under a 1s bound. On the old helper both reported status 0 after 8s, not a hang. On the new one both report 124 at about 1s. The 0089 fullcycle arm with `DEVBIN_TEST_TTY_PROMPT_WAIT=0` is now `not ok ... no [y/N] prompt within 0s` in 0s, not a hang. Only `run_tty_answer` uses expect. `run_tty_eof` gives `script` a `/dev/null` stdin, so a tty read gets EOF at once.

dc ran five mutants on a scratch copy, and the no-op control stayed green at 4 of 4. All five were killed:

| mutant                                   | result                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| prompt timeout silenced (`timeout { }`)  | KILLED by the prompt arm     |
| finish timeout silenced (`timeout { }`)  | KILLED by the finish arm     |
| kill and close dropped from `give_up`    | KILLED by both arms, by time |
| `exit 124` changed to `exit 1`           | KILLED by both arms          |
| the finish wait set from the prompt wait | KILLED by the finish arm     |

vc re-drove the 0 case and silenced the finish wait's `give_up` as a variant of its own. The finish arm killed it.
